This is Cascade Legal Rights Project. Thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond.

First, we understand why people are upset. Getting a letter from a law firm right after you asked someone for help is frightening, and it makes sense to wonder where they got your name. We'd be asking the same question.

Here is how we handle your information. We do not share, sell or disclose the names or details of anyone who attends our clinics. Our policy specifically bars giving attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Sign-in records stay inside our organization and are kept in locked storage.

Here is what we think is most likely happening. When a landlord files an eviction case in magistrate court, that filing is a public record. Some law firms pull names and addresses from those filings and send mailings to tenants. So a letter can show up whether or not the person ever came to a clinic or told anyone about their case.

We won't discuss any individual's situation here, even to answer what's been said about us. People who come to us are trusting us to keep it private, and that covers this thread too. If you've received one of these letters and want to talk about it, please contact us directly.

The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10am to 1pm, and everyone is welcome. That includes anyone who has doubts and would like to ask us questions in person. One change: the library meeting room is closed that day, so we've moved to the Mt. Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The time is the same. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible.

Questions can go to clinic@cascaderights.example, or you can call our office at 404-555-0187.
